title: Memory in .NET
units/0/blurb: What the operating system sees when .NET asks for memory: virtual addresses and pages, reserve and commit, why a process has several "memory used" numbers, the stack limit and CPU caches.
units/1/blurb: Working set, private bytes, commit and the managed heap are different numbers. What Task Manager, top and the GC APIs show; dotnet-counters, dotnet-gcdump, dotnet-trace, dotnet-dump and PerfView; how to find a leak with two snapshots and the path to a root.
units/1/source/title: Microsoft Learn: Debug a memory leak in .NET
units/2/blurb: What an object is made of: the header, the sync block and the MethodTable, how the CLR lays out and aligns fields, how arrays and strings sit in memory. The SOH, LOH and POH, regions in .NET 7+ and the .NET 8 non-GC heap.
units/2/source/title: Microsoft Learn: The large object heap
units/3/blurb: Why new in .NET is nearly free — a pointer bump in the thread's allocation context — and when it takes the slow path or goes to the LOH. Hidden allocations in closures, boxing, iterators, params, strings and async; ArrayPool, stackalloc, string.Create and measuring bytes per call.
units/4/blurb: What triggers a collection and how the generation is chosen, how threads are stopped at safepoints, marking from roots through GC info and the card table, the plan that picks sweep or compact, moving objects and updating references.
units/4/source/title: Book of the Runtime: Garbage collection design
units/5/blurb: Workstation and Server, background GC and the foreground collections that run during it, GCSettings.LatencyMode latency modes, DATAS in .NET 8–9, settings in runtimeconfig.json and environment variables, container limits.
units/5/source/title: Microsoft Learn: Garbage collector config settings
units/6/blurb: Finalization inside out: two queues, the finalizer thread, resurrection and SuppressFinalize. SafeHandle and critical finalizers, weak references and GCHandle, ConditionalWeakTable and leaks through closures, statics and timers.
units/7/blurb: Pinning and the pinned object heap, unsafe code, pointers and native memory, no-GC regions and the collector API, and what changes in memory under Native AOT without a JIT. The course final.
